clearance.min_gap_moving.measured_on: decided by the agent after a plate rubbed a turning pulley at 0.5 mm (one printer, 0.6 nozzle, PETG); never confirmed by a print or by the owner
clearance.min_gap_moving.description: least gap between a part and every neighbour that moves relative to it

clearance.scan_margin.description: how far round a part the gap probe looks for moving neighbours

clearance.gap_to_supported_face.measured_on: one printed carrier: 0.2 mm of running clearance to a roof printed over supports was not enough, about 1.2 axial worked (one printer)
clearance.gap_to_supported_face.description: running clearance to a face that was printed over supports

clearance.belt_wander.description: side room a belt needs for wander, on top of the gap

clearance.gap_over_foreign_head.description: clearance round a neighbour's screw head in the relief of a part that lies over it

clearance.sweep_step.measured_on: decided; a helper of one project stepped by 3 degrees, which can step over a rib
clearance.sweep_step.description: step of a sweep over the travel of a joint

clearance.sweep_step_near_stop.description: step of a sweep inside the fine zone before each stop

clearance.sweep_fine_zone.description: zone before each stop that is swept with the fine step

rules.title: Gap to every moving neighbour
rules.statement: A part keeps at least {clearance.min_gap_moving} to every neighbour of another declared motion group (printed, bought, hardware and mesh-only bodies within {clearance.scan_margin}), measured as the least distance in the pose as modelled. Clearance is a measured minimum gap, never "0 mm3 of overlap"; a coplanar pass counts as a collision. Parts that are fastened to each other move together and belong to one motion group: a gap of 0 between two groups is a collision or a wrong declaration. A mesh-only body is known by its bounding box: its box at the full gap or farther is a pass, its box nearer than that decides nothing and is reported as not checked, never as a failure. A part in no motion group is not measured, and the report says so for the part; the scan says it once for the document. The motion groups are declared in the layout of the project. The travel between the modelled poses is not covered here (clearance.sweep_full_travel).
rules.why: A motor plate was declared printable on "0 mm3 of overlap": its border hung 0.5 mm over the flange of a turning pulley and rubbed. The plate was reprinted several times in two days. The only tool measured overlap; gaps were printed ad hoc in three part scripts.
fix_order: Move the part or its neighbour apart.
Shape the moving feature so that it passes; do not carve the stationary part for it.
Cut this part back along the real envelope of the moving neighbour, to the full gap, and leave no thin ledge.
A gap that must be smaller: owner waiver that names the pair and the measured gap, with a hand test before power.

rules.title: No overlap with any neighbour in the static pose
rules.statement: Every new or changed part is intersected in the static pose with every neighbour, stationary against stationary too: hardware refs, heads of fasteners and ties, cables, springs and parts that exist only as meshes. Allowed overlaps are a named list with their expected volumes (an insert in its pocket, a press fit); anything else fails.
rules.why: Three new parts overlapped a neighbour by 4.6 to 7 cm3 for a day. A screw head sat 2.5 mm inside a printed part that existed only as a mesh. A mirrored ear landed on two screw heads. The helper that existed tested only the new tool body handed to it, and no mesh refs.
fix_order: Cut or move the new part.
An overlap that is meant (a press fit, an insert): add it to the named list with its volume.

attest.question: Was this part intersected with every neighbour in the static pose, hardware and mesh-only parts included?
labels: intersected with all neighbours: only the named overlaps
this part touches no other part

rules.note: Deferred: the gap probe measures other motion groups only. Overlap inside one group is not measured yet.

rules.title: Every joint is swept over its full travel
rules.statement: After every edit each affected joint is swept over its full travel and every adjustment position, both ends of a slide included. The list of fixed bodies is generated: every body that does not turn, the joint base included, never a hand-picked list. The step is {clearance.sweep_step}, and {clearance.sweep_step_near_stop} within {clearance.sweep_fine_zone} of each stop: a coarse step jumps over a rib. The hard stop is the first contact. A mechanism is checked at several phases. The gap in every pose is at least {clearance.min_gap_moving}.
rules.why: A sweep left the joint base out of its hand-picked list of fixed bodies: contact 1 degree before the stop. A 0.04 mm gap between a corner and a belt stood in a specification.
fix_order: Cut the part that meets first along the real envelope of the moving one.
Move the stop so that it is the first contact.

attest.question: Was every joint this part belongs to, or stands beside, swept over its full travel after the last edit?
labels: swept with a generated list of fixed bodies: the hard stop is the first contact
this part is in no moving joint and beside none

rules.note: Deferred: the gap probe measures the pose as modelled. A sweep with a cursor over the angles is not built.

rules.title: A mirrored feature is checked on its new side
rules.statement: A mirrored or moved feature is checked again against what exists only on the new side: screw heads, slots, cables. Where a part lies over a neighbour's screw heads it gets reliefs with {clearance.gap_over_foreign_head} round each head.
rules.why: A mirrored switch ear sat on two screw heads of the part below.
fix_order: Run the gate on the part after the mirror, with the neighbours of the new side placed.

rules.title: Shape the moving feature, not the stationary part
rules.statement: Do not carve a stationary part to let a moving feature pass: shape the moving feature. Nothing printed stands over a moving belt, and a belt gets {clearance.belt_wander} of side room for wander on top of the gap.
rules.why: A relief groove cut for a cam left a 1 mm ledge the owner found in the slicer. A plate border still stood over the belt after the first fix.
fix_order: Where the stationary part must give way: cut it back as a whole face, never as a groove.

rules.title: A face printed over supports needs a wider running gap
rules.statement: A running clearance to a face that was printed over supports is {clearance.gap_to_supported_face}, not the gap that works against a clean face (about 0.2): a face on supports comes out rough.
rules.why: 0.2 mm of clearance to a roof printed over supports was not enough on a printed carrier; the pocket was enlarged the same day.
fix_order: Widen the gap to the supported face.
Turn the part so that the running face prints clean, on the bed or as a top face.

rules.title: Unconfirmed clearances get a hand test
rules.statement: Every clearance under the gap rule that no print has confirmed is listed with a hand test: the joint is turned through its whole travel by hand before power is applied.
rules.why: No incident of its own: it is the bench half of the gap rule. The rub that paid for the gap rule was found only when the joint turned.
fix_order: Put the hand test into the build notes of the joint.
